title: federation: one domain, many mailboxes
description:
Spec: jmap-chat-spec 03f4318/77532f9/38a200b (bead jmap-chat-spec-f82v), BREAKING for -00. draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00 now lets one peer domain host many mailboxes.
Wire changes:
- Every Peer/* call (deliver, receipt, typing, retract, groupUpdate, subscribePresence, unsubscribePresence, presence) gets a REQUIRED recipientUserId (String): identity of the target mailbox owner on the receiver; receiver routes to the mailbox whose ownerUserId equals it (octet match). Single value; batch several recipients as several method calls in one signed request (MAY).
- accountId in Peer/* now = the id of the ONE peer-role account; the peer-role Session MUST have exactly one account regardless of user count.
- Caller-identity fields (senderUserId, readerUserId, subscriberId, identity) now name the user on the calling server. Each MUST bind to the authenticated peer domain: host == peer domain; host-less (did:key) only via DID-bound verification; else reject the call with forbidden.
- Unknown recipientUserId: reject with forbidden, SHOULD be identical (incl. description) to a forbidden on an existing mailbox.
- Presence subscriptions keyed by (subscriberId, recipientUserId).
- Discovery Session: ownerUserId no longer MUST. Single-mailbox server SHOULD include it (and MAY ownerDirectAddress/ownerEndpoints); multi-mailbox server omits all three. A peer SHOULD apply owner metadata only if ownerUserId binds to the Session domain.
- chat-00: ownerUserId is MUST in the Session served to an authenticated owner (federation servers); relay routing args include recipientUserId.
Tests: jmap-chat-compliance-tests.md 7.16 (rewritten), 7.18, 7.20 (new) are the oracle.

crate-jmap work: crate-jmap-chat-federation-server Peer/* handlers (recipientUserId routing, per-field host binding, uniform forbidden for unknown recipient, single peer account), presence subscription key, discovery Session ownerUserId optional; outbound side in crate-jmap-chat-server (outbound.rs, presence.rs) sends recipientUserId and batches per domain; base-client types. Breaking: release as 0.5. kith and chinwag consume it.
notes:
Mark decided 2026-10-30: include a 'testkit' feature in jmap-chat-server for 0.5: backend tests as generic async fns over B: ChatBackend plus a macro emitting #[test]s; MemoryBackend runs them through the macro; chinwag runs them against its SQLite backend (chinwag-nuqe.25).
Mark decided 2026-10-30: also include sender_id on OutboundEvent::Receipt in 0.5 (chinwag-nuqe.7.20: under burnOnRead in a group chat the Message is gone before the event, so the server cannot address the Peer/receipt). Server-side PushSubscription (JMAP-nbk3) is NOT in 0.5.
From JMAP-7x4p (commit 3754041a): crate-jmap-chat-federation-types/tests/draft_examples.rs round-trips every c08568e Peer/* example; recipientUserId currently lands in extra. When this lands, add typed recipient_user_id assertions there and drive the examples through the federation-server handlers, including the Error Handling forbidden example (recipientUserId nobody@bob.example, fed c08568e L1248-L1275), which the 0.4 handlers cannot reproduce because they ignore recipientUserId.
